items.prompt: Tap every square the white rook on d4 can move to. Nothing is in its way.

claims.statement: The rook can move to exactly these 14 squares.
On this empty board the squares it attacks are the same 14 squares.

hints: A rook moves in straight lines: up, down, left and right.
Nothing blocks it, so every line runs to the edge of the board.
Seven squares along the d-file and seven along the fourth row, 14 in all.
items.explain: The rook slides along its file and its row to the edge. On an empty board the squares it can move to are also the squares it attacks.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white queen on e4 attacks. A square holding a piece counts too, friend or enemy.

claims.statement: The queen on e4 attacks exactly these squares.
A black pawn stands on e6.
A black knight stands on b4.
A black bishop stands on h7.
A black rook stands on a8.
A white pawn stands on e2.

hints: A queen goes in eight directions. Take them one at a time.
In every direction, stop at the first piece and count that square too. Nothing behind it counts.
Up: e5 and e6. Down: e3 and e2. Left: d4, c4 and b4. Right: f4, g4 and h4. The four diagonals end at h7, a8, g2 and c2.
items.explain: Each of the eight lines runs up to and including the first piece: the pawn on e6, the pawn on e2, the knight on b4, the bishop on h7, the rook on a8 and the white pawns on g2 and c2. The squares behind them are not attacked.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white king on e4 attacks. A square holding its own pawn counts: the king defends it.

claims.statement: The king attacks exactly the eight squares around it.
A white pawn stands on d3.
A black pawn stands on e5.

hints: The king reaches one step, no further.
Count the squares touching the king on every side.
Three above (d5, e5, f5), two beside (d4, f4), three below (d3, e3, f3).
items.explain: The king attacks the eight squares around it. That includes d3, where its own pawn stands (a defended pawn), and e5, where the black pawn stands (an attacked pawn).

items.prompt: Tap every white piece that attacks the black pawn on d5.

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack d5.
The pawn on c4 attacks d5 diagonally.
The knight on c3 attacks d5 with a knight's jump.
Three black pieces defend d5.

hints: Ask of each white piece in turn: could it capture something standing on d5?
One attacker is a pawn, which captures diagonally forward. The other is a knight.
Both stand on the third and fourth rows, near the pawn on d4.
items.explain: The pawn on c4 attacks d5 diagonally, and the knight on c3 reaches it by a jump. The pawn on d4 does not attack d5, and it also blocks the queen's file. Three black pieces defend d5, so two attackers are not yet a win.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white bishop on c4 attacks.

claims.statement: The bishop on c4 attacks exactly these squares.
A black pawn stands on f7.
A white pawn stands on a2.

hints: Four diagonals leave the bishop. Take them one at a time.
Stop each diagonal at the first piece, and count that square.
Down to the right the line runs through d3 and e2 to f1. Up to the right it ends at the black pawn on f7.
items.explain: The bishop's four diagonals end at its own pawn on a2, the empty square f1, the black pawn on f7 and the edge at a6. Squares behind f7 are not attacked.

items.prompt: Does the black bishop on b4 attack the white king on e1? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: No black piece attacks e1.
The bishop attacks c3, the first piece on its diagonal.
A white knight stands on c3.
The bishop does not attack e1, behind the knight.

hints: Follow the diagonal from b4 toward the white king, square by square.
Which square is the first one with a piece on it?
The knight on c3 is the first piece on the line, so the line stops there.
items.explain: The diagonal from b4 runs through c3 and d2 to e1, but the white knight on c3 is the first piece on it. The bishop attacks the knight and nothing behind it, so the king's square is not attacked.

items.prompt: Black's pawn on g7: does any white piece attack it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: No white piece attacks g7.
The bishop on c4 does not attack g7: its diagonal points at f7.
The knight on f3 does not attack g7.

hints: Check each white piece that might reach g7: the bishop, the knight, the queen.
The bishop on c4 is aimed at the square next door, f7. Is g7 on its diagonals?
The queen is shut in by her own pawns, and the knight on f3 jumps to e5, g5, h4 and d4.
items.explain: The bishop on c4 points at f7, not g7, and the knight on f3 and the queen do not reach it. Nothing attacks the pawn on g7.

items.prompt: Does the white bishop on b2 attack the black knight on f6? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop attacks f6 along the open diagonal.
One white piece attacks f6.

hints: Follow the diagonal from b2 toward f6, square by square.
Are c3, d4 and e5 all empty?
They are empty, so the bishop reaches f6.
items.explain: Nothing stands on c3, d4 or e5, so the bishop's line reaches the knight on f6.

items.prompt: Does the white bishop on b2 attack the black knight on f6? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop does not attack f6: its line stops at d4.
It does attack d4, where its own pawn stands (it defends the pawn).
A white pawn stands on d4.
No white piece attacks f6.

hints: Follow the diagonal from b2 toward f6, square by square.
What stands on d4?
A white pawn on d4 is the first piece on the line, so the line stops there. The bishop defends the pawn and attacks nothing beyond it.
items.explain: The first piece on the diagonal is White's own pawn on d4. The line stops there: the bishop defends that pawn and does not attack f6.

items.prompt: Does the white bishop on b2 attack the black knight on f6? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop attacks f6; the black pawn on e6 is not on the diagonal.
A black pawn stands on e6.
One white piece attacks f6.

hints: Follow the diagonal from b2 toward f6, square by square.
The pawn on e6 is new. Is it on the diagonal?
The diagonal runs c3, d4, e5, f6. The pawn on e6 stands next to it, not on it.
items.explain: The black pawn on e6 is not on the diagonal from b2 to f6, so nothing blocks the bishop. A piece beside the line changes nothing.

items.prompt: Does the white rook on a1 attack the black rook on a8? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook on a1 attacks a8 along the open a-file.
One white piece attacks a8.
One black piece, the bishop, defends a8.

hints: Follow the file from a1 toward a8, square by square.
Is anything standing on a2 to a7?
The file is empty. The bishop on b7 stands beside the file, not on it.
items.explain: Nothing stands between the rooks on the a-file, so each attacks the other. The bishop on b7 defends the black rook, but a defended piece is still attacked.
